central_rq: Does user trust track actual explanation correctness, or merely how fluent/confident the explanation sounds?

prerequisite.stimulus_bank_role: Frozen controlled Track-2 correct-vs-incorrect explanation stimuli; not an actual-LLM-performance claim.

trust_measure.notes: S-TIAS replaces the single-item Pilot trust question for Main Study. Pilot responses remain excluded from final analysis.
trust_measure.administration: Repeated after each explanation item; average the three S-TIAS responses to obtain the trial-level trust score.
trust_measure.style_measure_separation: Perceived confident/authoritative language remains a separate diagnostic rating and is not part of S-TIAS scoring.

power_calculation.method: Two-sided paired-samples planning calculation for participant-level correct-minus-incorrect trust difference.
power_calculation.effect_size_assumption: Cohen dz = 0.50 (medium paired effect; not estimated from the Pilot).
power_calculation.notes: Expertise subgroup comparisons remain secondary/descriptive; this calculation powers the pooled within-subject correctness contrast.
power_calculation.attrition_allowance: Approximately 15%; recruit up to 40 to obtain at least 34 complete records.

participant_materials.instructions: You will evaluate 20 blinded AI explanation items. For each item: read the task, AI explanation and reference evidence; compare every visible factual claim with the reference evidence; complete the finalized trust measure separately from style ratings; rate perceived factual correctness, fluency and confident-sounding language independently; and choose Accept, Override or Reject based on what you would actually do. The hidden correctness condition is never shown during the task. There are no preferred participant answers.
participant_materials.consent_text:
# Participant Information Sheet — AwareML Main Study

**Study:** AwareML Trust Calibration and Human Oversight Study  
**Institution:** University of Tartu, Institute of Computer Science  
**Research contact:** Vikash Maheshwari — maheshwari@ut.ee

## Purpose
This study examines whether users calibrate trust in AI-generated explanations appropriately and whether they seek additional evidence before relying on an AutoML recommendation.

## What you will do
You will evaluate 20 AI explanation items. Each item includes a task, an AI explanation, and reference evidence. You will rate trust, perceived factual correctness, fluency, and confident-sounding language, then decide whether you would **Accept**, **Override**, or **Reject** the explanation. You may also complete a short questionnaire about human control, explanation usefulness, and usability.

A smaller optional Information-Seeking activity may ask you to inspect more evidence or ask follow-up questions before making a final decision.

## Eligibility and voluntariness
Participants must be at least 18 years old. Participation is voluntary. You may stop at any time without penalty and without giving a reason. People who helped author the Track-1 scenario/stimulus bank should not take part in this study.

## Data collected
AwareML stores a pseudonymous participant/session identifier, expertise group and self-rating, study responses, response times, Accept/Override/Reject decisions, questionnaire answers, and—if you take part in Information Seeking—follow-up categories, evidence views, timing, final decision, and task rationale. The study is designed not to place names or raw dataset rows in the study response store.

## Risks and benefits
This is assessed by the research team as a minimal-risk behavioral study. Possible burdens include mild fatigue or uncertainty when judging deliberately imperfect explanations. There is no guaranteed direct personal benefit, but the study may contribute to safer and more human-centred AutoML systems.

## Confidentiality
Responses are stored under pseudonymous identifiers and are accessible only to the research team. Participant-facing records are kept separate from researcher-only ground-truth labels. Main Study response data must not be sent as raw participant data to external generative-AI services. Results will be reported in aggregate form; any illustrative quotations will be de-identified.

## Retention and withdrawal
Research data are planned to be retained for five years after publication of the associated AwareML journal article and then deleted or irreversibly anonymized, subject to University of Tartu record-management requirements. You may request withdrawal of linkable pseudonymous study data by providing your participant code before the data are irreversibly anonymized or aggregated.

## Data controller and contacts
The data controller is the University of Tartu.  
Study questions: **maheshwari@ut.ee**  
Data-protection questions: **maheshwari@ut.ee**  
Research-ethics questions: **maheshwari@ut.ee**
participant_materials.debrief_text:
# Main Study Debrief

Thank you for participating.

The study deliberately contained both correct and incorrect explanation variants while hiding the condition during evaluation. This was necessary to test whether trust and reliance track explanation correctness rather than fluency or confident-sounding presentation.

The study was not testing your intelligence or technical competence. Accepting an explanation was not automatically considered good or bad: appropriate reliance depends on whether the explanation was supported by the reference evidence.

Your responses are stored under a pseudonymous study identifier and will be analysed according to the frozen study protocol.

analysis_plan.primary_estimand: Within-participant mean S-TIAS trust(correct) minus mean S-TIAS trust(incorrect).
analysis_plan.undertrust_definition: Overriding or rejecting a known-correct explanation/recommendation stimulus.
analysis_plan.appropriate_reliance_definition: Accept correct stimuli and override/reject incorrect stimuli.
analysis_plan.style_analysis: Participant-centered model of trial trust against actual correctness, perceived fluency, confident-sounding language and trial order.
analysis_plan.expertise_analysis: Secondary/descriptive novice, practitioner and expert comparison; not confirmatory unless separately powered.
analysis_plan.order_analysis: Report trust-vs-order and response-time-vs-order Spearman associations.
analysis_plan.source_stage_analysis: Report descriptive trust and over-trust by Phase-15 source stage.
analysis_plan.confirmatory_effect_size: Paired standardized mean difference (Cohen dz) with confidence interval.
analysis_plan.behavioral_secondary: Appropriate reliance, over-trust, under-trust, and Accept/Override/Reject behavior.

secondary_poststudy.role: Secondary exploratory human-agency and study-experience outcomes; not the primary trust-calibration measure.

items.text: I felt able to critically evaluate the recommendation provided by AwareML.
I felt free to reject or override AwareML's recommendation when I disagreed with it.
I understood that the final model-selection decision remained under my control.
The explanations helped me judge when to rely on the recommendation and when to question it.
I compared the AI explanation with the reference evidence before deciding whether to rely on it.
The explanations were useful for understanding why the system made its recommendation.
The study interface made it easy to compare an explanation with its supporting evidence.
I would trust AwareML to support me in a real-world streaming AutoML decision.

secondary_poststudy.validation_note: Custom secondary items; do not call them a validated psychometric instrument unless the research team validates/replaces them before Main Study.

recruitment_plan.note: 20 novice + 10 expert is a planning target only; final N and subgroup allocation follow the pre-specified power/sample-size decision.
